name: Cardiac Amyloidosis ATTR Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for ATTR Cardiac Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of transthyretin amyloid deposits in cardiac tissue by biopsy or non-invasive imaging
Echocardiographic evidence of increased left ventricular wall thickness with restrictive cardiomyopathy pattern
Identification of pathogenic TTR gene mutation (for hereditary ATTR)
Positive 99mTc-PYP or DPD bone scintigraphy with grade 2 or 3 myocardial uptake in absence of monoclonal protein
Exclusion of AL amyloidosis by serum and urine immunofixation and free light chain assay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cardiac amyloid deposits confirmed by biopsy or positive bone scintigraphy with typical echocardiographic features and exclusion of AL amyloidosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing distinguishes hereditary from wild-type ATTR amyloidosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Restrictive cardiomyopathy with preserved ejection fraction
searchTerms: stiff heart muscle with normal pumping
heart muscle restriction with good ejection

pathognomonic.symptomName: Conduction system disease with atrioventricular block
searchTerms: heart electrical disease with AV block

pathognomonic.symptomName: Low voltage on ECG despite increased ventricular wall thickness
searchTerms: low ECG voltage despite thick heart walls
weak ECG signals with thick heart muscle
reduced ECG amplitude with ventricular thickening

common.symptomName: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction symptoms
searchTerms: symptoms of heart failure with normal ejection
breathlessness and fatigue with preserved heart function
heart failure signs despite normal pumping

occasional.notes: More common in AL amyloidosis but can occur

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated cardiac biomarkers (troponin, NT-proBNP)
Absence of monoclonal protein in serum and urine
Elevated serum transthyretin in hereditary cases
imaging: Echocardiogram showing increased left ventricular wall thickness with granular sparkling appearance
Cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement and abnormal T1 mapping
99mTc-PYP or DPD bone scintigraphy showing myocardial uptake
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in TTR gene (e.g., Val122Ile, Thr60Ala, Val30Met)
other: Endomyocardial biopsy with Congo red staining showing apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Electrocardiogram showing low voltage QRS complexes and conduction abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
More frequent involvement of kidneys and soft tissues
Family history of sarcomeric gene mutations

redFlags: Rapidly progressive heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Unexplained increased ventricular wall thickness with low ECG voltage
History of bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome preceding cardiac symptoms
references: Maurer MS, et al. 'Transthyretin Amyloidosis: An Underdiagnosed Cause of Heart Failure.' J Am Coll Cardiol. 2016.
Ruberg FL, et al. 'Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiac Amyloidosis: A Systematic Review.' JAMA. 2019.
Gillmore JD, et al. 'Nonbiopsy Diagnosis of Cardiac Transthyretin Amyloidosis.' Circulation. 2016.
